title: Community colleges: elected Chicago board (City Colleges)
lastAction: Co-sponsor added; still pending in Senate Assignments
summary: Would replace the mayor-appointed City Colleges of Chicago board of trustees with an elected board, starting with the 2027 consolidated election. The General Assembly would divide Chicago into 20 trustee districts for the board seats.
effect: City Colleges (District 508) only. City Colleges is the only community college district in Illinois without an elected board.
nextStep: Senate Assignments must send it to a committee for a hearing.

title: Academic Freedom of Expression Act
lastAction: Senate Floor Amendment No. 4 re-referred to Assignments
summary: Creates the Academic Freedom of Expression Act. It states that faculty at public colleges and universities have the right to freedom in teaching, freedom in research, and freedom of expression on matters of public concern. Colleges would file their academic freedom policies with the Illinois Community College Board or the Board of Higher Education.
changes: The Senate Executive Committee passed it as amended in March 2026. Later Senate floor amendments (through No. 6) recast it as a change to the Public Higher Education Act, with policies due by July 1, 2027.
effect: All 14 colleges. Community colleges would file their policies with the Illinois Community College Board.
nextStep: Must be released from Senate Assignments for a Senate floor vote.

title: Meaningful Human Control of Artificial Intelligence Act
lastAction: Re-referred to Rules Committee
summary: Creates the Meaningful Human Control of Artificial Intelligence Act. Public employers could not rely on automated decision-making systems for decisions about workers' employment, benefits or rights without meaningful, continuing human review. It adds transparency and bias-audit requirements, anti-retaliation protections, Department of Labor enforcement and a right to sue.
changes: Amended in the House Labor & Commerce Committee, which passed it 18–9 in March 2026.
effect: Applies to public employers; whether college districts are covered depends on the final text.
nextStep: Must be released from House Rules for House floor votes (second and third reading).

title: Meaningful Human Review of Artificial Intelligence Act
lastAction: Re-referred to Rules Committee
summary: Creates the Meaningful Human Review of Artificial Intelligence Act. State agencies could not use automated decision-making systems for public benefits, individual rights or similar decisions without continuous review by a trained person who can override the system. Agencies would have to complete impact assessments first.
effect: Applies to State agencies; whether community college districts count depends on the definitions.
nextStep: Must be released from House Rules and heard in a committee.

title: Operating Room Safety Act
lastAction: Added as Alternate Co-Sponsor (Senate)
summary: Creates the Operating Room Patient Safety Act. Surgical technologists hired or contracted by hospitals and surgical centers would have to meet education, certification or experience requirements. Some rural and safety-net facilities are exempt.
effect: Colleges that run surgical technology programs.
nextStep: Must be assigned to a Senate committee and pass it, then a Senate floor vote.

title: OER grant program for academic libraries ($3 million)
lastAction: Added Co-Sponsor
summary: Appropriates $3 million from the General Revenue Fund to the Secretary of State for a recurring, permanent grant program for Illinois academic libraries. The grants would go toward open educational resources.
effect: Academic libraries, including those at the 14 colleges.
nextStep: Must be released from House Rules and heard in an appropriations committee.

title: Library grants: OER grant program ($3 million)
lastAction: Referred to Assignments
summary: The Senate version of the $3 million open educational resources grant program: a recurring appropriation to the Secretary of State for grants to Illinois academic libraries.
effect: Academic libraries, including those at the 14 colleges.
nextStep: Senate Assignments must send it to a committee for a hearing.

title: Digital Library Protection Act
lastAction: Added as Alternate Co-Sponsor (Senate)
summary: Creates the Digital Library Protection Act. Publishers could not license e-books and digital audiobooks to libraries on terms that restrict normal library operations, such as checkout limits. Violations would count as consumer fraud, and Illinois law would govern the contracts.
changes: House Amendment No. 1 (April 2026) replaced the bill's text before the House passed it 99–0–1.
effect: Covers academic libraries, including community college libraries.
nextStep: Must be assigned to a Senate committee and pass it, then a Senate floor vote.

title: Digital Library Protection Act (conforming change)
lastAction: Referred to Rules Committee
summary: A companion bill making a related change to the Digital Library Protection Act. It has not moved since it was filed.
nextStep: Must be released from House Rules and heard in a committee.

title: Unemployment Insurance: labor dispute
status: On House calendar, 2nd Reading - Short Debate
lastAction: Added Co-Sponsor (Nov. 17: Rules approved the bill for consideration and returned it to the 2nd Reading calendar)
summary: Changes the Unemployment Insurance Act so that workers idled by a labor dispute are ineligible for benefits for no more than 2 weeks, instead of for every week of the dispute.
changes: On Nov. 17 the House Rules Committee recommended House Floor Amendment No. 2, which would replace the bill's text.
nextStep: House floor: second reading, where Floor Amendment No. 2 can be adopted, then a third-reading vote.

title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
lastAction: Became Public Law No. 119-75
summary: The fiscal 2026 federal spending law, signed Feb. 3, 2026. It kept the maximum Pell Grant at $7,395 for 2026–27 and level-funded TRIO ($1.2 billion) and Strengthening Community Colleges Training Grants ($65 million).
effect: Student aid and federal grants at all 14 colleges.
nextStep: None; it is law (Public Law 119-75). Fiscal 2027 education funding is in separate bills now before Congress.

title: Student Loan Borrower Bill of Rights
lastAction: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions
summary: Sets servicing and disclosure standards that apply to both federal and private student loans, such as rules for how payments are handled. It lets the Education Department adjust the standards for federal loan servicers.
effect: Student loan borrowers, including students and employees at the 14 colleges.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
lastAction: Referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
summary: Would halt construction or upgrading of AI data centers nationwide until Congress passes laws giving the federal government oversight of AI, including protections for workers, consumers and communities.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act (House companion)
lastAction: Referred to Energy and Commerce and to Foreign Affairs
committee: House Energy and Commerce; Foreign Affairs
summary: House companion to the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act: a nationwide pause on new and upgraded AI data centers until federal AI safeguards become law.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the House Energy and Commerce Committee (also referred to Foreign Affairs).

title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026
lastAction: Referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
summary: Would permanently ban building or deploying artificial superintelligence and pause the most advanced AI development until a new federal Department of AI sets safety rules. It directs the United States to seek international agreements against superintelligence.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026 (House companion)
lastAction: Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
summary: House companion to the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence, a pause on the most advanced AI development, and a new federal Department of AI.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

title: AI Tax and Work Protection Act
lastAction: Referred to Education and Workforce and to Ways and Means
committee: House Education and Workforce; Ways and Means
summary: Would tax large AI companies on the higher of the value of AI tokens they sell or their AI product revenue, with rates that rise with unemployment. The money would fund a new Work Protection Administration in the Labor Department that awards job-creation grants.
effect: Includes added Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) funding.
nextStep: Hearings or markups in House Education and Workforce and House Ways and Means.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
lastAction: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance
summary: Creates an AI Horizon Fund, paid for by taxes on the AI industry, for worker training, service jobs and support for workers whose jobs are lost to AI. A 15-member advisory council that includes labor, higher education and workforce experts would guide the spending.
nextStep: A hearing or markup in the Senate Finance Committee.

title: Community college baccalaureate degree programs
lastAction: Added Co-Sponsor (Apr. 17: re-referred to House Rules Committee under Rule 19(a))
summary: Amends the Public Community College Act so a community college board can offer applied bachelor's degree programs in fields with a documented, unmet workforce need, if the district shows it has the expertise, resources and student demand. Programs need approval from the Illinois Community College Board and the Board of Higher Education. Districts must report each year, and the state must evaluate the programs within five years.
effect: Any Illinois community college district could apply, including City Colleges (District 508) and the 7 suburban districts; the bill groups districts into regions.
nextStep: Back in the House Rules Committee: Rules must approve it for floor consideration, then House second and third readings.

title: Community college baccalaureate degree programs (Senate version)
lastAction: Added as Co-Sponsor
summary: The Senate version of the community college baccalaureate bill: it would let community college boards offer applied bachelor's degree programs in high-demand fields, with state approval, annual reports and a five-year statewide evaluation.
effect: Any Illinois community college district could apply, including City Colleges (District 508) and the 7 suburban districts.
nextStep: Senate Assignments must send it to a committee for a hearing.
